courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: So with Firebase setup, let's go back to our code and let's have a look at our place
service. There, we have our addPlace method and thus far
what we do here is we add that place to our local list of places.
Now of course we can do that but I also want to store that place on the server now because that is the
whole idea of having a back-end,
this will allow the places to survive even if the user restarts the app or uninstall it or anything
like that,
it of course also is necessary to share places between users.
So how do we store our data on a server then?
Well, remember we're building an Angular app here and in Angular, you have the HttpClient to communicate
with back-ends and therefore, we'll use that here.
Now to use that, you should check that in your app module, you do actually add a special new import and
I'll add it here at the start and that is the HttpClientModule.
Now the HttpClientModule here needs to be imported from @angular/common/http,
so from this path here. This is required to unlock the injectable HttpClient which we then can inject
into our various modules and components wherever we need it to send HTTP requests.
So we add this import here and add HttpClientModule to the imports array in the app module and with that
back into places service, we can go to the start of this service, here to the constructor and now not
just inject the auth service but our own HttpClient or I'll just name the property HTTP
here but the name is up to you, our own HttpClient service which is provided by Angular.
So you do inject the type, HttpClient here and HttpClient is imported from
@angular/common/http and that is now a service provided by Angular,
so built into Angular that you can use to send HTTP request.
Now we want to use that here in addPlace of course, we're creating our new place object here and we want
to store that on a server.
Now actually what I don't want to build here or what I don't want to construct here is the ID though, instead
Firebase will generate a new ID for us and I want to use that since that will then be a real guaranteed
unique ID and therefore, I want to send the place without the ID to Firebase. Now how can we do that?
There are various ways, one of the easier ways is to simply copy that place object and replace the ID
with null when we're sending this.
So let's start setting this by accessing this HTTP and now for Firebase and probably for a lot of REST
APIs, if you want to create something, you send a post request and with Angular's HttpClient, you do
that by using the post method here.
Now you first of all need to enter the URL to which you want to send the request and that would be
this URL you find here in your Firebase real-time database, so I add it here but then and that's the
special and nice thing about Firebase, you add your own segment here to give the folder so to say under
which the data should be stored a name. Right now, we have no folders here, it's empty down there because
we haven't added anything but that will soon change.
So I will name this offered-places but the name is up to you
and now a special thing about Firebase, you always need to add .json at the end,
this is not required by Ionic or by Angular,
this is really just a Firebase URL thing,
if you are using a different REST API, you probably don't have to add this.
So this is the URL,
the second argument in this post method then is the data we want to send and here I'll create a new Javascript
object and copy all the properties of new place but I'll overwrite the ID property then and set this
to null and this will essentially then not store it on Firebase because I don't want to store my ID
there, I want to instead let Firebase generate a new ID and then use that. Now Angular, as in many other
places uses observable behind the scenes when working with HTTP requests.
So in the end what I can do here is I can return this and now we can subscribe to that anywhere where
we want to start this because it will not send the request before a subscription has been set up but
also where we want to listen to that. Just one thing of course is I still want to have my
places here and update my places whenever we're basically done adding this. Therefore we'll have to combine
this places observable to which we're listening with our HTTP observable here.
Hence I will add the pipe method here at the end of my HTTP request chain and in that pipe method,
I now can work with the result of this first observable,
so basically with the response of this HTTP request. For a start, let's simply have a look at that
and therefore here I will add tap,
I will have my response data in here and I will simply console log the response data. So temporarily,
our app will be broken,
I will comment out this unnecessary return statement here. It's important that you still return this
HTTP request though so that your other code where you subscribe to that observable from inside the
component,
so in our case from inside the new offer page component, that this code still works, this subscription
here, the subscribe method call only works if addPlace returns an observable, which it does right now.
So let's give this a try,
let's save everything and let's have a look at our application here.
Let's go to offers and let's add a new offer, test does this work,
the price and some dates here of course, like that and submit this and this looks pretty good.
It finished, it showed us the loading spinner so something took place,
remember that we commented out our own observable chain, that we commented out our delay in place
service, so this here is clearly not what caused the spinner to show up and here on the right, you see that
console log and that is the response by Firebase,
this is essentially the unique ID it generated.
It gives you an object with a name field and that holds the unique ID
and if we have a look at Firebase here, this should live update, you now see this new offered places
node here and in there, you see that same unique ID
and under that ID, you have the data for your place which is pretty nice of course.
